To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Bayesian regularization method is a useful tool for the identification of structural damage.
the regularization methods can be used to identify structural damages and the regularization parameter can be estimated from the available data.
the regularization parameter is a function of the noise level in the measurement data and of the level of the structural damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues:   1.
the development and application of regularization methods for identification of structural damage.
development of new regularization methods for identification of damage in structural systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
regularization methods are very useful in the identification of structural damage.
regularization techniques are useful in obtaining a minimum energy solution of an ill-posed problem.
the Bayesian approach is the only one which can provide the unique (minimum energy solution) to a modified and well-conditioned problem and thus can provide an accurate estimate of structural damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of regularization methods in the context of damage detection and identification has been successful in providing a unique and physically meaningful solution to the inverse problem.
the regularization parameter (penalty parameter) is the key to the solution of the inverse problems, and that it is important to determine the optimal value of this regularization parameter.
the Bayesian approach is very useful in the identification of structural damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regularization methods can be used in conjunction with the Bayesian approach to estimate damage parameters in structural systems.
the regularization parameter is not a constant, but rather a variable which depends on the data.
the Bayesian regularization is a powerful technique for the solution of ill-posed problems.
